# Project Brief — Backyard Garden Suite (Hempcrete)

Prepared by: Dana Hartley (owner / builder)   Date: 2026-10-14

Site: 0000 Example Avenue NW, Edmonton, AB (fictional address)   Legal description: don't have it yet — will ask the city (fictional)

Permit #: not applied for yet

# What I want to build

A small one-bedroom garden suite at the back of my lot for my mother. About 60 m² main floor, with a sleeping loft over the bathroom. I think that makes it under 3 storeys, but I'm not sure how lofts are counted.

# The unusual part

Instead of a normal 2x6 stud wall with batt insulation and poly, I want 300 mm cast-in-place hempcrete around a timber frame (2x4 at 600 mm o.c. buried in the hempcrete), finished with lime render outside and lime plaster inside. No poly vapour barrier — the supplier says hempcrete needs to "breathe".

- Roof: conventional trusses, blown cellulose, standard shingles

- Foundation: insulated slab on grade

- Heating: one ductless heat pump + electric baseboard backup

- Distance to house: about 4 m; to back lane fence: about 1.5 m

# What I have

- Supplier brochure "HempWall Pro" (fictional) claiming R-2.0 per inch and "excellent fire resistance"

- Photos of a similar build in BC

- No lab tests, no engineer yet

# Questions

Do I need a variance? What do I have to give the city? Can I do this without hiring an engineer?

# Project brief: Example Commons, firestop issue on L3–L4

**From:** Carlos Mendes, PM, Northgate Example Builders Ltd. *(fictional)*  **Date:** 2026-10-15

## Project
| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Name | Example Commons *(fictional)* |
| Address | 0000 Example Avenue SW, Calgary, AB *(fictional)* |
| Legal | Lot 0, Block 0, Plan 0000000 *(fictional placeholder)* |
| Owner | Example Commons Holdings Inc. *(fictional)* |
| Building permit | BP-0000-00000 *(fictional)*, issued |
| Building | 5 storeys, sprinklered, retail at grade, 64 dwelling units above |
| Design team | Example Architecture Inc. *(fictional)*, coordinating registered professional; Example MEP Engineering *(fictional)* |
| Floor assemblies | Rated fire separations. *Rating per the architect's code analysis: "1 h"* |

## What happened
Our firestop sub sealed the plumbing penetrations on L3 and L4 with **Example FireSeal 200** *(fictional)* and handed in listing **EX-FS-1234** *(fictional)*. The third-party firestop inspector says that listing only covers **metal pipes**. Ours are mostly **PVC drain pipe and bundles of PEX**, and some holes are bigger than the listing allows. L2 (copper) passed.

The sprinkler fitter used the same sealant around the sprinkler branch lines. The sub says sprinklers are "exempt".

## What we need
- Keep the **drywall close-in on 2026-10-24**
- Ideally "a variance so we don't have to rip it out"
- We have a **draft EJ email** from the sealant rep

## Who we've talked to
- Architect (email attached). Not yet the City inspector.
